text.p: Here are highlights of stories reported by Hungary's press, based on information by Nepszabadsag's Hungary Around the Clock service. For further details on how to subscribe to Hungary Around the Clock, please contact Monica Kovacs at (361) 351 2440 or fax your request to (361) 351 7141.
ALL PAPERS
- A top official of the coalition Free Democrats kicked off Monday's parliamentary session by criticising the Slovak Parliament's recent ban on foreign national anthems in public. @
- Prime Minister Gyula Horn has postponed his appointments for this week, having come down with the flu Sunday night.
- Hungary and Turkey have finalised the text of a free trade agreement based on the former country's association agreement with the European Union.
MAGYAR HIRLAP

- The International Monetary Fund remains confident in Hungary's economic management so far this year, the Fund's representative in Hungary, Mark Allen said at the close of a week-long visit by an IMF delegation.

- Next year's state subsidies for local governments and the Interior Ministry were increased by HUF30 billion and 8 billion respectively and the Industry and Trade Ministry will also receive more: HUF1.8 billion for tourism, 4.8 billion for technical development and 6 billion to promote investment. The government foresees agriculture subsidies of HUF 88-90 bilion next year.
- The State Debt Management Centre will issue state bonds with a variable interest on October 10, deputy director Laszlo Borbely said.
- A committee of judges assigned to check the backgrounds of public figures to root out those who worked for internal security forces under the communist regime will begin their work next week.

- The Christian Democrats decided to send protest telegrams to the US Ambassador to Budapest and the US State Department regarding a joint commentary in the Washington Post and the International Herald Tribune concerning the basic treaty between Hungary and Romania.
- Hungary and several regional states began a series of joint exercises Monday under the aegis of NATO's Partnership for Peace programmes.
- The ailing state broadcasting company Antenna Hungaria has issued bonds worth HUF 2.2 billion.
- Hungary joined the West European gas pipeline last weekend by hooking up with the Austrian system.
- Debrecen will play host to an international UFO conference this comming weekend.
NEPSZABADSAG
- President Arpad Goncz will pay a state visit to Sweden on October 1-3.

- A consortium led by the private French station TF1 and the German group Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitungsverlags gesellschaft will announce its intent to bid in the prospective tender for Hungarian Television's channel two.
VILAGGAZDASAG
- The balance of payments deficit was $33 million in July, less than the monthly averge of the previous two quarters, according to a report from the National Bank.
- The State Privatisation and Holding Co. plans to complete the first round of the privatisation of the agricultural producer Babolna Rt this year.
- An open tender will be called to sell off 100 per cent of Fotaxi, Hungary's largest taxi firm.
NAPI GAZDASAG

- The Hungarian Investment and Development Bank will increase the HUF 700 million ($4.45 million) subscribed capital of the china factory Zsolnay by ECU 720,000 ($903,000) at the firm's general meeting late this month.
-- Budapest newsroom (36-1) 327 4040
